currentlyReading.title: Political Order and Political Decay
currentlyReading.description: I am currently reading on institutions, state capacity, and long-term political development.

books.title: Diario de motocicleta
books.author: Ernesto Guevara de la Serna
books.summary: Funny, surprising, and much more enjoyable than expected.

books.title: El laberinto de la soledad
books.author: Octavio Paz
books.summary: Deeply thoughtful, clear, and remarkably concise while still covering an enormous amount.

books.title: A City Dreaming
books.author: Daniel Polansky
books.summary: One of the funniest books I have read in years. Uneven in a few chapters, but overall a brilliant and inventive take on the wizard-in-New-York trope.

books.title: Gli italiani
books.author: Luigi Barzini
books.summary: Excellent in parts, especially on theatricality, institutional weakness, and the adaptive fluidity of Italian society. Clearly written for foreigners and for a very specific period.

books.title: El complot mongol
books.author: Rafael Bernal
books.summary: Begins almost absurdly, then turns sharp and unexpectedly profound. Strong character work in a short space, with surprising depth and momentum.

books.title: Aura
books.author: Carlos Fuentes
books.summary: Striking atmosphere and style, though it did not fully land for me.

books.title: El señor presidente
books.author: Miguel Ángel Asturias
books.summary: Devastating and emotionally overwhelming. A vivid portrayal of dictatorship, moral collapse, and human hardship, with language that powerfully mirrors the brutality of the world it depicts.

books.title: Confabulario
books.author: Juan José Arreola
books.summary: A mixed collection for me: some stories are exceptional, while others felt heavy and less convincing.

books.title: Pedro Paramo
books.author: Juan Rulfo
books.summary: Mexico most emblematic book. Brings to an extreme the combination of simplicity and complexity while showing the soul of a nation.

books.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
books.author: Gabriel García Márquez
books.summary: Arguably the best novel ever written.

books.title: The Story of a Shipwrecked Sailor
books.author: Gabriel García Márquez
books.summary: Good entry to the work of Gabo. Can be dry at times but it does show his journalistic roots

books.title: Kitchen Confidential
books.author: Anthony Bourdain
books.summary: As a former cook, the raw and colourful representation of such a world depicted by Bourdain remains probably, if not the most realistic, the most consequential.

books.title: Neuromancer
books.author: William Gibson
books.summary: Understandably a fundational novel of modern CyberPunk. The lingo hits hard at times

books.title: Men Explain Things to Me
books.author: Dan Wang
books.summary: Amazing beginning with catchy first chapters. Moving towards moralizing/academic at the end

books.title: Breakneck: China's Quest to Engineer the Future
books.author: Dan Wang
books.summary: Fresh change of perspective from liberal/authoritarian to lawyer/engineer societies. Uniquely balanced analysis of the current geopolitical situation. As a European, the concept of Europe as mausoleum economies felt reductive and too eager to push a bidimensional view of world order.

books.title: Revolusi: Indonesia and the Birth of the Modern World
books.author: David Van Reybrouck
books.summary: Comprehensive description of Indonesia's colonial past. The end can be quite heavy and excessively leaning towards a moralizing stance.

books.title: The Dispossessed
books.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
books.summary: Best book of the year. Rarely does a novel give me so much to think about power, gender, economics, and the craziness of the world we live in.
